unit.title: Colors and Describing Words: Los Colores

lesson.title: Mis Cosas Favoritas: Write Three Describing Sentences
lesson.subject: spanish

contentBlocks.text: Guessing games are done. Now you are the describer, on paper. Pick three things you like and write one Spanish sentence about each — the color, and what you think of it.

Two words for what you think of how something looks: [[bonito]] — pretty, nice-looking — and [[feo]] — ugly, not nice-looking. Both change to match the noun: bonito/bonita, feo/fea.

Mi dibujo es bonito.
Mi mochila es bonita.
El monstruo del cuento es feo.
La casa vieja es fea.

Here is your sentence frame. Use it three times:

Mi + (thing) + es + (color) + y + (bonito/bonita, feo/fea, or brillante)

Mi cuaderno es azul y bonito.
Mi regla es verde claro y bonita.
Mi bicicleta es roja y brillante.

Watch the endings. Cuaderno is an 'el' word, so bonito. Regla is a 'la' word, so bonita. Brillante and any claro or oscuro shade never change.

Choose three things you own or like — una mochila, un lápiz, una bicicleta, una camiseta, un cuarto. Write one sentence about each with the frame. Make at least one of them use a light or dark shade (claro or oscuro). Then read all three aloud to a parent or partner.
Three sentences, each with a color and an opinion, all the endings matching. Tomorrow you draw an arcoíris — a rainbow — and present it at a class art gallery.

items.prompt: Write in Spanish: 'My notebook is blue.' (notebook = el cuaderno)
Write in Spanish: 'My backpack is purple and pretty.' (backpack = la mochila)
acceptedAnswers: mi mochila es morada y bonita
mi mochila es morada y bonita.

items.prompt: Write in Spanish: 'My ruler is light green.' (ruler = la regla)
Write in Spanish: 'My bike is red and shiny.' (bike = la bicicleta)
acceptedAnswers: mi bicicleta es roja y brillante
mi bicicleta es roja y brillante.

objectives: Write three sentences with the frame Mi ___ es (color) y (bonito/bonita, feo/fea, or brillante)
Match bonito/feo to the noun (bonito with an 'el' word, bonita with a 'la' word)
Keep the color after the noun and keep brillante and claro/oscuro unchanged
materialsNeeded: Three favorite objects, or the child's memory of them
A parent or partner to read the finished sentences aloud to
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review es + color + y + word from yesterday with one spoken example: Es azul y brillante.
2. Teach bonito and feo, showing both endings: Mi dibujo es bonito / Mi mochila es bonita.
3. Write the frame on paper: Mi ___ es (color) y (bonito/bonita, feo/fea, brillante). Fill it in together for one object the child owns.
4. The child picks three things and writes one sentence each. Coach the endings: check the article of the noun, then match bonito/feo; leave brillante and claro/oscuro alone.
5. The child reads all three aloud, slowly.
6. Play the translate activity — type each English sentence in Spanish.
7. Complete the worksheet (the child's own three sentences, neatly).
8. Preview tomorrow: draw and present a rainbow.
differentiationTips: Struggling: pre-write two of the three frames with the noun and article filled in, so the child only chooses the color and the opinion word
Ready for more: add a fourth sentence that describes something the child thinks is feo, and a fifth that contrasts two things ('Mi lápiz es amarillo, pero mi mochila es azul oscuro')

For the teaching adult: the most common error will be a mismatched ending ('mi mochila es bonito'). Point back to the article — la mochila, so bonita. Brillante ends in -e and claro/oscuro are invariable as shade words, so none of those three ever changes
This is a writing task, so it does not depend on the audio-recording gap noted elsewhere (open decision, expansion-plan-2026-09.md §12.9) — the read-aloud only needs a listener
teacherGuide.answerKey: Frame: Mi ___ es (color) y (bonito/bonita, feo/fea, brillante). Model sentences: Mi cuaderno es azul y bonito. Mi regla es verde claro y bonita. Mi bicicleta es roja y brillante. Translate activity: 1. Mi cuaderno es azul. 2. Mi mochila es morada y bonita. 3. Mi regla es verde claro. 4. Mi bicicleta es roja y brillante. A correct child sentence has the color after the noun, the changing color and bonito/feo matching the noun's gender, and brillante / claro / oscuro left unchanged.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Day 4 in the scope-and-sequence is 'write three sentences describing favorite objects, using es + color + adjective.' This is presentational writing under WA-WL-2015.1.3: the child produces original, memorized-plus-adapted sentences — exactly the Novice Mid target the 3-5 band notes describe — and the write-then-read-aloud step rehearses Friday's spoken presentation. Requiring the endings to agree turns Tuesday's word-order rule into something the child applies unprompted rather than just recognizes.
